minutes.headline: Assessors heard a stormwater task force pitch a new utility fee shifting costs onto big paved lots
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors approved minutes from six earlier meetings and heard a lengthy presentation from a resident representing the town's stormwater task force on a proposed stormwater utility fee meant to close a DPW budget gap and meet EPA mandates, which would shift more cost onto large paved commercial/industrial properties. The board also reviewed the neighborhood-reclassification project's timeline (deferred to spring), got an update that the new principal assessor has been ratified and starts August 18th, and discussed raising the veterans' property tax exemption for a possible November town meeting warrant article rather than September. No substantive item beyond the minutes and adjournment was decided by a formal, counted vote.

what_happened.line: A resident presenting for the town's stormwater task force pitched a new utility fee that would shift more cost onto large paved commercial and industrial lots, and asked assessors for property data to help design it.
The board tabled a proposed increase to the veterans' property tax exemption for the September town meeting, aiming instead for a November warrant article to give more time to inform the public.
Reclassification of waterfront and lakefront neighborhoods will not change any tax bill before spring; the work continues only in a test copy of the assessing database.
The board noted the town's new principal assessor has been ratified by the select board and starts August 18th.

why_it_matters: A stormwater utility fee would be a new charge outside the property tax levy, and the task force's design would weight it toward large paved commercial and industrial properties rather than spreading it evenly.
A veterans' exemption increase is paid entirely by local taxpayers through the overlay account, with no state reimbursement, and would need town meeting approval to take effect.
Waterfront and lakefront property owners will not see any billing change from the reclassification project until at least spring, regardless of what the test database shows now.
